1:1.sourceText: Ὁ πρεσβύτερος ἐκλεκτῇ κυρίᾳ καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις αὐτῆς, οὓς ἐγὼ ἀγαπῶ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ, καὶ οὐκ ἐγὼ μόνος ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἐγνωκότες τὴν ἀλήθειαν,
1:1.targetText: The elder to the chosen lady, and to her children, whom I love in truth, and not only I, but also all those having known the truth,

1:2.sourceText: διὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν τὴν μένουσαν ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ μεθ’ ἡμῶν ἔσται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.
1:2.targetText: because of the truth that is remaining in us, and will be with us throughout the age,

1:3.sourceText: ἔσται μεθ’ ἡμῶν χάρις ἔλεος εἰρήνη παρὰ Θεοῦ Πατρός, καὶ παρὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Πατρός, ἐν ἀληθείᾳ καὶ ἀγάπῃ.
1:3.targetText: there will be with you grace, mercy, [and] peace from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father, in truth and love.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual Greek ἡμῶν is us, not the second-person you in LSV; the difference is not a matched pronoun.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV has the second-person you where pinned N1904 has first-person us.
English supplies a conjunction within the grace/mercy/peace list; Greek lists the three nouns without it.
The Lord title is additional source-witness wording in LSV; N1904 has Jesus Christ without this title.

1:4.sourceText: Ἐχάρην λίαν ὅτι εὕρηκα ἐκ τῶν τέκνων σου περιπατοῦντας ἐν ἀληθείᾳ, καθὼς ἐντολὴν ἐλάβομεν παρὰ τοῦ Πατρός.
1:4.targetText: I rejoiced exceedingly that I have found of your children walking in truth, even as we received a command from the Father;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:5.sourceText: καὶ νῦν ἐρωτῶ σε, κυρία, οὐχ ὡς ἐντολὴν γράφων σοι καινὴν, ἀλλὰ ἣν εἴχαμεν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, ἵνα ἀγαπῶμεν ἀλλήλους.
1:5.targetText: and now I implore you, lady, not as writing to you a new command, but which we had from the beginning, that we may love one another,

1:6.sourceText: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἀγάπη, ἵνα περιπατῶμεν κατὰ τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ· αὕτη ἡ ἐντολή ἐστιν, καθὼς ἠκούσατε ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, ἵνα ἐν αὐτῇ περιπατῆτε.
1:6.targetText: and this is love, that we may walk according to His commands; this is the command, even as you heard from the beginning, that you may walk in it,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:7.sourceText: ὅτι πολλοὶ πλάνοι ἐξῆλθον εἰς τὸν κόσμον, οἱ μὴ ὁμολογοῦντες Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐρχόμενον ἐν σαρκί· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ πλάνος καὶ ὁ ἀντίχριστος.
1:7.targetText: because many deceivers entered into the world, who are not confessing Jesus Christ coming in flesh; this one is he who is leading astray, and the antichrist.

groups.note: Greek πλάνος is the nominal/adjectival deceiver or misleading one, paraphrased as the agent who is leading astray. The additional relative-clause copula is supplied separately.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual N1904 ἐξῆλθον means went out, whereas LSV entered reflects the different inward-motion reading; the opposite-direction verbs are not paired.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV entered differs from N1904 went out (ἐξῆλθον); the directional source-witness difference is retained.
English supplies is in its relative verbal paraphrase of the nominal/adjectival πλάνος; the actual earlier ἐστιν belongs to this one is.

1:8.sourceText: βλέπετε ἑαυτούς, ἵνα μὴ ἀπολέσητε ἃ ἠργασάμεθα, ἀλλὰ μισθὸν πλήρη ἀπολάβητε.
1:8.targetText: See to yourselves that you may not lose the things that we worked for, but may receive a full reward;

1:9.sourceText: πᾶς ὁ προάγων καὶ μὴ μένων ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ Θεὸν οὐκ ἔχει· ὁ μένων ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ, οὗτος καὶ τὸν Πατέρα καὶ τὸν Υἱὸν ἔχει.
1:9.targetText: everyone who is transgressing, and is not remaining in the teaching of the Christ, does not have God; he who is remaining in the teaching of the Christ, this one has both the Father and the Son;

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 has προάγων, going ahead/beyond, rather than the transgressing verb reflected in LSV. Their related contextual warning is not treated as identical lexical wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV transgressing reflects the different παραβαίνων reading rather than N1904 προάγων, going ahead/beyond; the lexical witness difference is explicit.
The second of the Christ qualification is repeated in LSV but absent after the second teaching in the pinned N1904 wording.

1:10.sourceText: εἴ τις ἔρχεται πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ταύτην τὴν διδαχὴν οὐ φέρει, μὴ λαμβάνετε αὐτὸν εἰς οἰκίαν, καὶ χαίρειν αὐτῷ μὴ λέγετε·
1:10.targetText: if anyone comes to you, and does not bear this teaching, do not receive him into the house, and do not say to him, “Greetings!”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:11.sourceText: ὁ λέγων γὰρ αὐτῷ χαίρειν κοινωνεῖ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ τοῖς πονηροῖς.
1:11.targetText: For he who is saying to him, “Greetings,” has fellowship with his evil works.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:12.sourceText: Πολλὰ ἔχων ὑμῖν γράφειν οὐκ ἐβουλήθην διὰ χάρτου καὶ μέλανος, ἀλλὰ ἐλπίζω γενέσθαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ στόμα πρὸς στόμα λαλῆσαι, ἵνα ἡ χαρὰ ἡμῶν πεπληρωμένη ᾖ.
1:12.targetText: Having many things to write to you, I did not intend [it] with paper and ink, but I hope to come to you, and speak mouth to mouth, that our joy may be full.

groups.note: The actual writing action is first expressed by to write, then resumed as the bracketed object of I did not intend [it] with paper and ink. It is the same intended act; there is no separate Greek pronoun.
Greek γενέσθαι, to become/be present, denotes coming to be with the recipients in this complete visit construction; English renders the arrival idiom as to come.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

1:13.sourceText: Ἀσπάζεταί σε τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἀδελφῆς σου τῆς ἐκλεκτῆς.
1:13.targetText: The children of your chosen sister greet you. Amen.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: The closing Amen is additional LSV source-witness wording, absent from pinned N1904.
